title: An Old Ape Fossil Found in Egypt
summary: Scientists have found a very old ape fossil in Egypt. It may change what we know about where apes, and humans, first came from. The new ape is called Masripithecus moghraensis. It lived about 17 to 18 million years ago. Its bones were found at Wadi Moghra in northern Egypt. It is the first true fossil ape ever found in North Africa. A team from Egypt and the University of Southern California wrote about the find in the journal Science. For a long time, scientists thought early apes lived mostly in southern Africa. North Africa had given us old monkey fossils, but never an ape. This find may fill that gap. "We spent five years searching for this kind of fossil," said Hesham Sallam, a scientist at Mansoura University. The ape belongs to a group called crown Hominoidea. Only the ape's lower jaw was found. The jaw is very strong, with big canine teeth. The ape probably ate mostly fruit, but its strong teeth could also crush nuts and seeds.
why_it_matters: Finding old bones helps us learn where we came from, like solving a puzzle about your own family.

keywords.explanation: A fossil is the remains of a living thing from long ago.
Crown Hominoidea is the group of all living apes and their shared ancestors.
Canine teeth are the sharp, pointed teeth near the front of the mouth.
A jaw is the part of the face that holds the teeth.
To crush means to press something hard until it breaks.
A journal is a magazine where scientists share new findings.
